editorial:
If you like horror that mixes dark humor with creepy doll chaos, this asylum-set sequel gives you a wild ride. Nica is locked away and made to doubt her own memories, while a Good Guy doll turns group therapy into a nightmare. The movie keeps the Chucky attitude alive with sharp one-liners, bloody surprises, and a tense hospital setting that feels scary without being too heavy. It also gives Nica more room to fight back, which makes the chaos feel personal.

The acting, especially Fiona Dourif and Brad Dourif's voice work, keeps the story fun, and the pacing moves fast enough to hold your attention. Some kills feel familiar and the plot gets silly, but fans of the series will enjoy the callbacks and the bold ending. If you want a gory, playful horror night, this is a good pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Chucky reveals he can split his soul into more than one doll. He uses voodoo to take over Nica's body, so she walks out acting like Chucky while Tiffany drives away with a Good Guy doll. Andy is left trapped in the asylum, and the last moments show Chucky is free in a dangerous new form.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slasher sequels with dark humor.
